newsitem.title: CHINA: China July flooding hit crude oil production.
newsitem.headline: China July flooding hit crude oil production.

text.p: Devastating floods that swept across parts of China in July caused major damage to oil wells, resulting in production losses of more than 280,000 tonnes of crude, the Xinhua news agency said on Wednesday.
The flooding had forced 46,000 well closures at 21 onshore oilfields and had damaged equipment, instruments, pipes, power lines and roads linked to the oil industry, the agency said.
Production from eastern oilfields fell by 270,000 tonnes in January to August compared with a year ago, it said, adding that eastern oil output declined by 520,000 tonnes in 1995.
Oil output from western China in the first eight months rose by 1.40 million tonnes compared with the year-ago period, the agency said.
National oil production was now averaging 388,000 tonnes per day and output for all of 1996 was forecast to total more than 141 million tonnes (2.82 million barrels per day), Xinhua said.
China's oil output was 105.21 million tonnes in the first eight months of the year, with production in August reaching 13.31 million tonnes, official statistics show.
